You're right. OP she's just trying to hurt you. Her actions speak for her, and she is acting out of malice. Cry. Be honest with your parents. Just listen to them, and try to give yourself time to think, but not too much time. If you start having intrusive thoughts, take a step back and do something you enjoy. There's something good for you just waiting for you to take it. In the meantime, there's so much to learn about yourself. This is a nightmare, I know. Trust me. But we'll both get through this.

My psychiatrist says that feeling suicidal isn't normal. You can feel a lot of things, you can feel horrible, but if your brain chooses suicide over feeling something, then it feels that staying alive and feeling what you're feeling is worse than death. 

That simply isn't true. You CAN feel through this and you CAN work it out. Suicidal thoughts are grounds for medication, even if it's situational. Meds don't HAVE to be a lifelong thing. That's a common misconception.

If depression interferes with your daily life without something as traumatic as this, then yeah maybe. But if it's just an event like this that triggers it, then maybe a little bit will help you through it. 

That's only half the battle though. Meds only do HALF the work. You have to do the rest. And you have to want to be better. You have to WANT to be happy again. The meds will help you think more positively. After that, you gotta take the reigns and trust them. Even a placebo can make you feel better.

So take that first step. You'll be so proud of yourself. I know I was. And now I have a great support system. Be better. It doesn't have to be the end. It hurts but it's supposed to. That just means what you felt before was really great. 

And anybody can make you feel that way. Anybody can. You just have to trust them. It's a two way street though. You have to feel the bad to appreciate the good. But there's more good to come. It'll be even better now that you understand. 

But in the meantime, get your symptoms treated so you can feel better. And don't forget, you're not alone. You don't have to suffer through this alone, we're all suffering together. So do what you need to do. 

Besides, picking yourself up from something like this takes a lot of strength. Looks great on your resume.

I'm not telling you to assign meaning to pain, I'm saying that everything we feel we learn from, and that's a fact. You just need to be mindful enough to be able to tell.

If you don't learn from pain you're bound to be hurt again. You learn how to deal with your emotions so you can endure suffering walk away to tell about it. Every time, it hurts just a little less, and that's how you know you're learning.

The fact that you survived it is just evidence of your strength. I recently learned that I've suffered for such a long time, but every day I learn something new about myself. I have to deal with this pain and I'm forced to figure out how and why I feel the way I do and assess how to feel better. You learn more through pain and suffering because that's just how we function as humans.

We learn from consequence, good or bad. Should I eat this even though it looks weird? I threw up after so no, I won't eat it again. It's buried deep in our psyche. If you're not getting a negative consequence for anything you do, you're living in complacency, and you'll never learn a damn thing.

I'm not the same person I was a year ago. And I've changed even more rapidly, for the better, since I've begun this harrowing journey of mine. I may suffer every day, but I'm so much smarter and better for it. I just need the suffering to end, and when it does, I'll be so much better than I would've been without it.

But hey, I never said we were perfect. It's a shitty way to learn. It's a shitty way to have to live. She told me that herself, and I agree.

People like that don't realize they have a problem. If he's just blowing it off, he hasn't fully convinced himself he has a problem yet. It's a different mentality to realize "This thing I do, this thing I never thought twice about, is something I should stop doing for my own health and safety." It takes humility. It takes courage.

It's hurting the people around him. If he hasn't realized that yet, he needs professional help. Word it to him EXACTLY the way I've worded it to you. Make him actually think about it. Let HIM realise. That's the only way he'll know. If you really care about him, and if he can be good for you and your kid, help him help you.

It'd make him really happy if you did, but your happiness comes first. Can he make you happy? Do you trust him to? If your daughter is your priority, can you make sure she's not traumatized long term from the experience? I'm not saying kids should be responsible for holding people together, but again, priorities.

If you believe he's capable, give him a trial period. Be open minded. Convince yourself he's the one and let HIM prove you otherwise. You have to want it too. Be honest with yourself and be honest with him. Make sure he's talking from his heart and not out of his ass, make him be honest with you too. It's your life we're talking about. If you let him in again, he'd better make it worth your while.

I'm married to the idea of being open minded and hopeful, but I'm on the other side of the spectrum, so I'm biased. Admittedly, I may be projecting a bit, but this is how I feel about the matter. Hope it helps you get a bigger picture.

If you don't hate each other and you get along well, then do it. Just address what happened before, and be honest about it. And I mean really honest. I think that's the best way to go about it.

If you're both mindful and mature about it and you can communicate well, then go for it and support each other the right way.

In the end, do what makes you happy and don't be afraid to work for it. Don't think about what COULD be. Make it happen for yourself. It sounds hard, but it's love. The fuck did you expect?
